Closing for API redesign. A special `layerWithHostConfig({ unavailableTools })` constructor is the wrong abstraction; tool visibility should follow the existing permission/catalog model. We will replace this with a smaller permission-based design.

Closing rather than continuing to revise this implementation. Independent lifecycle and Effect-v4 reviews found that the current approach remains incomplete: AppProcess.runStream still waits on inherited-pipe EOF, generic cancellation can remain unbounded for TERM-resistant children, the production-shaped regression fails consistently on macOS, and post-exit process-group cleanup has PID/PGID reuse risk. A replacement will use Effect-native scoped drains and will be opened only after deterministic red-green-red proof across the production Session seam.

> This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
> - #30662: Auto session title generation fails for opencode provider models (smallOptions missing provider config) — directly related to the title agent ignoring small_model/provider config
> - #26658: Main LLM call never executes. Session stuck on thinking after title generation. — similar symptom of the session being blocked after the title agent runs
> - #29734: Session title generation silently fails with no fallback or logging — related title agent failure with no user-visible error
> 
> If your issue is distinct from those (e.g. the `FreeUsageLimitError` retry loop blocking the main model is a separate compounding factor), please add a note clarifying the difference so maintainers can track it appropriately.

Clarification re: potential duplicates
After reviewing the referenced issues:
#30662 — Related but distinct. That issue is about smallOptions() missing provider config for opencode models, causing silent failure. My issue is about small_model config being ignored entirely — the title agent always uses deepseek-v4-flash-free regardless of what’s configured, even when the model would otherwise work.
#26658 — Different root cause. In that issue the main model call never executes at all (deadlock). In my case, the main model does execute, but only after the title agent exhausts its FreeUsageLimitError retry loop (~90s backoff). The session eventually responds — just with a 90-second delay before the first token.
#29734 — Closest overlap. My issue adds two things that #29734 doesn’t cover: (1) the reason title generation fails is that small_model config is hardcoded away — not just that it can fail, and (2) the failure mode isn’t just a silent ignore — it’s an active ~90s block on the main model because FreeUsageLimitError is marked isRetryable: true and the title agent retries 3× with backoff before Effect.ignore kicks in. That retry window is what blocks the session thread.
The compounding factor specific to my report: title agent + main model share the same session thread, so the 90s retry loop visibly delays every first response even when the main model has zero issues.

Additionally, even after the free quota reset (no more 429s), response times remain ~135s with kimi-k2.6 as the main model and no errors in logs. This confirms the 2-minute delay has a second independent cause beyond the retry loop: server-side latency on opencode.ai/zen/v1 post-1.16.0 release, evidenced by EIO: i/o error, write exceptions in the worker logs. The title agent bug and the server load are compounding separately.

The server-side lag predates 1.16.0 — I was already seeing 2+ minute response times on 1.15.x starting Thursday June 4, before updating. This suggests the latency is load-related rather than a regression in 1.16.

Following up on the dictionary-completeness ask with a related correctness note on the `prefix()` logic itself (`packages/opencode/src/permission/arity.ts`), since the two interact:

Beyond *which* commands are listed, the prefix-extraction has two cases where the "human-understandable command" it derives diverges from the real command:

1. **Flags between the command and subcommand aren't skipped.** `prefix(["git", "--no-pager", "commit"])` walks longest→shortest, matches `git` (arity 2), and returns `["git", "--no-pager"]` — so a rule scoped to `git commit` never sees `commit`. The generator rule says "Flags NEVER count as tokens," but the extractor doesn't strip them.
2. **Unlisted commands collapse to the first token**, so wrapper/prefix forms hide the real command: `["bash", "-c", "…"]` → `["bash"]`; an inline env-assignment prefix (`CI=true git commit`) becomes the identity. This looks like the same root behind #16075.

So expanding the dictionary helps the listed cases, but a flag-skipping / wrapper-aware extraction step would address the class.

Worth noting: MCP OAuth servers deployed behind AWS WAF with `AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet` will reject requests containing `http://127.0.0.1` URLs in the body or query parameters. The `GenericRFI_BODY` and `GenericRFI_QUERYARGUMENTS` rules flag IP-literal URLs as potential Remote File Inclusion attacks and return 403 Forbidden.

This affects both Dynamic Client Registration (`redirect_uris` in the JSON body) and the authorization redirect (`redirect_uri` query parameter) when the redirect URI uses the `127.0.0.1` form.

[RFC 8252 §7.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8252#section-7.3) recommends using `localhost` rather than IP literals for loopback redirect URIs in native OAuth apps. Using `http://localhost:...` avoids triggering these WAF rules entirely.

Relevant AWS docs: [AWS Managed Rules - Common Rule Set](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/aws-managed-rule-groups-baseline.html)

It would be good to make sure the default redirect URI in this refactor uses `localhost` rather than `127.0.0.1` to avoid this class of issues.

In case someone else still has this issue like me, gemma4 suggested me to add this skill to opencode, seems to work so far:
```md
---
name: precise-edit
description: Use ONLY when performing file edits to ensure maximum reliability and minimum token waste.
---

# Precise Edit Workflow

To avoid "corrupt patch" errors, "off-by-one" line number failures, or the token waste of full-file rewrites, always follow this strict workflow when modifying code:

## The Workflow

1. **Read**: Use the `read` tool to get the most current version of the file.
2. **Extract**: Identify the exact, byte-for-byte string that needs to be replaced. This includes all indentation (tabs/spaces) and newlines.
3. **Edit**: Use the `edit` tool with the exact string as `oldString`.
    - **NEVER** guess line numbers.
    - **NEVER** assume the content of the file based on previous turns.
    - **NEVER** provide a "shorthand" or "roughly correct" string.
4. **Verify**: Run a compile check (e.g., `cargo check`, `npm run typecheck`) immediately after the edit.

## Why this is preferred
- **Reliability**: Using the exact string from a fresh `read` ensures the `edit` tool finds the match.
- **Token Efficiency**: It avoids the massive token cost of a full-file `write`.
- **Safety**: It prevents "corrupt patch" errors associated with manual diff construction.

## Examples

**Incorrect (Guessing):**
`edit(filePath="src/main.rs", oldString="fn main() {", newString="fn main() {\n    println!(\"hello\");")` $\rightarrow$ High risk of failure if indentation differs.

**Correct (Precise):**
1. `read(filePath="src/main.rs")` $\rightarrow$ sees `"12: fn main() {"`
2. `edit(filePath="src/main.rs", oldString="fn main() {", newString="fn main() {\n    println!(\"hello\");")` $\rightarrow$ Guaranteed success.
```
Edit:
you can also ask the LLM about how to improve the skill whenever the edit fails or causes another compile failure. For me it added the following to the workflow:
```md
    - **CRITICAL**: If an `edit` fails, you MUST call `read` again to synchronize with the current file state before retrying. **NEVER** use the `write` tool as a fallback for a failed `edit`.
    - **Scope Check**: When replacing a block of code, explicitly identify all variables defined within that block. Ensure they are either preserved or redefined in the `newString` to avoid scope errors.
    - **Atomic Logic**: Ensure the `newString` is a self-contained logic unit that does not rely on variables deleted during the replacement.
```

I'm encountering the same issue in Kilo Code. Using deepseek-v4-flash via the built-in DeepSeek provider (BYOK), image attachments are blocked client-side before any API call is made.

The DeepSeek API itself supports image inputs for deepseek-v4-flash (it uses a ViT encoder with ~90 KV-cache entries per image). The problem is entirely in OpenCode's protocol-level check:

packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts:192-193 hardcodes ["text"] as the only allowed content type
The model's modalities/capabilities definition is never consulted for content-type validation
A proper fix would be to make the content-type check in openai-chat.ts aware of the active model's declared capabilities, rather than hardcoding ["text"]. The models.dev entry for deepseek-v4-flash already has modalities.input: ["text"] — updating that to include "image" is also needed, but without the protocol fix it would have no effect.

Use case: Analyzing UI screenshots, architecture diagrams, and error messages in screenshots during coding sessions — which works in Claude Code and other tools but is broken here for DeepSeek V4 Flash users.

Would love to see this addressed. Happy to test a fix if one is proposed.
